makerFinancing.name: Apple Card Monthly Installments (ACMI)
makerFinancing.eligibility: Qualified customers with an Apple Card, subject to credit approval and limit. The iPhone must be bought with AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon selected as carrier; prepaid carrier plans are not allowed (so not Mint Mobile). The phone is unlocked. Tax and shipping go on the card at its variable APR, not 0%.

makerFinancing.name: Apple Upgrade Lease (provided by Klarna Inc.)
makerFinancing.eligibility: Consumer lease, not a purchase or loan; US residents only; must select an eligible carrier, not prepaid; approval based on creditworthiness; 12- and 36-month terms not available for all models; early termination can cost up to the remaining lease payments; insurance not included.

makerFinancing.name: Apple financing provided by Affirm
makerFinancing.eligibility: On approved credit for iPhone purchases over $99. Current monthly offers table: iPhone 0.00% for 24 months (iPad 4.99%/12, Mac 7.99%/24). Taxes and shipping paid in full at time of purchase.

makerFinancing.name: Flexible Finance Account (Creation Consumer Finance Ltd)
makerFinancing.eligibility: Subject to eligibility, application and status; a reusable line of credit brokered by Apple Retail UK Ltd. 0% APR offer on the terms shown per model. Representative 14.9% APR variable applies to other terms (example: £1,200 over 12 months at 14.9% = £107.72/month, £92.73 interest).

carrierFinancing.method: Loan through Affirm, chosen at checkout; paying in full up front is the other option. Mint does not lend itself.
carrierFinancing.zeroPercent: Depends on credit; Affirm's own published range is 0-36% APR. Affirm's 'Pay in 4' (four payments over six weeks) is 0% APR.
carrierFinancing.requiresCarrierPlanNote: Mint's iPhone 17 page says the new-customer offer 'Requires separate purchase of new device on and 12-month Mint plan (sold separately)'. Mint does not say whether an Affirm loan on its own needs a Mint plan.
carrierFinancing.phonesLocked: Phones bought from Mint are unlocked after 60 days active on Mint's network.
carrierFinancing.note: Mint's help page confirms financing through Affirm but publishes no term lengths or APR. The 0-36% range is Affirm's general disclosure and was not read off a Mint checkout. Mint's site returns 403 to direct fetches, so it was read through the r.jina.ai reader.

carrierFinancing.method: None. Public Mobile sells no phones and offers no device financing. It is bring-your-own-phone only ('All you need to bring is your own phone').
carrierFinancing.note: In Canada, a phone on installments has to come from the maker (Apple through Affirm) or a retailer, not from Public Mobile.

carrierFinancing.method: Amigo Paguitos: an Amigo Kit (prepaid phone) paid in weekly instalments, arranged in person at a Telcel Customer Service Centre or authorised distributor. Telcel sets the down payment when it approves the application, and the buyer picks the term.
carrierFinancing.requiresCarrierPlanNote: Amigo Paguitos sells Amigo Kits, which are Telcel prepaid lines. The requirements are a current INE, an active mobile number and an email address. No guarantor or credit history is needed.
carrierFinancing.note: Telcel publishes no interest rate, CAT, term lengths or down payment for Amigo Paguitos. They are set at the point of sale. Telcel's prices include 16% IVA.

carrierFinancing.method: Interest-free months (meses sin intereses, MSI) on participating bank credit cards in the Telcel online store, including iPhone.
carrierFinancing.monthsNote: Telcel's Apple page says only 'meses sin intereses con tarjetas participantes'. Hola Telcel's Hot Sale 2026 post (25 May to 2 June 2026) offered up to 24 MSI, with BBVA terms of 6-9 and 12-24 months. The months available outside promotions are not published.
carrierFinancing.requiresCarrierPlanNote: Telcel does not say whether an MSI purchase in the online store has to come with a Telcel line.

carrierFinancing.method: Klarna loan ('pay monthly'): the buyer chooses an upfront payment and a plan length, and gets an instant decision. giffgaff is a credit broker; Klarna Bank AB is the lender. Paying outright needs no credit check.
carrierFinancing.monthsNote: SIMsherpa (16 July 2024) says 'a 12, 24 or 36-month contract'. One search snippet attributed to giffgaff's help centre gives 6-36 months. giffgaff's current help page says only that a term may be unavailable if Klarna declines it.
carrierFinancing.zeroPercentNote: Third-party summaries describe giffgaff's Klarna loans as 0% APR interest-free, but no giffgaff page read for this research states an APR.
carrierFinancing.requiresCarrierPlanNote: Non-members buying a new phone must buy a non-refundable one-off SIM plan of at least £10 with the phone. It does not apply to refurbished devices in good, very good or excellent condition. The SIM need not be activated, and the phone can be used on another network.
carrierFinancing.phonesLocked: All giffgaff phones are unlocked and stay unlocked.
carrierFinancing.note: Refurbished phones from giffgaff are sold through the same Klarna checkout. giffgaff's pay-monthly SIM contracts last 18 months, with an early termination charge of half the plan price times the months left. That contract is for the SIM, not for the phone loan.

carrierFinancing.method: Bill Pay phones: the handset is bundled into a Bill Pay plan, with an upfront handset price (for example 'Free' for a Samsung Galaxy S25 FE, or from €649.99 for an Apple iPhone 17 Pro on a given plan) plus the monthly plan charge. There is no separate handset instalment loan. Prepay phones are bought outright.
carrierFinancing.monthsNote: 'Offers subject to availability, a Bill Pay Plan and a minimum term of 24 months.'
carrierFinancing.note: Upfront prices depend on the plan, and Clubcard prices are lower. The page lists Bill Pay plans from about €20 to €60 a month, but its per-plan handset prices were not captured. tescomobile.ie refuses direct fetches, so it was read through WebFetch's summariser and the figures should be checked by eye.

activation.activationFeeNote: No activation fee appears in Mint's plan terms. Third-party guides (moneysavingpro.com) also say Mint charges none. The terms do allow a reactivation fee after a suspension, with no amount stated.
activation.simKitNote: The SIM or eSIM comes with the prepaid plan purchase (Mint sells the service in 3-, 6- and 12-month blocks), and no standalone starter-kit price was found on mintmobile.com.
activation.esimReplacementNote: The first five eSIMs in any 12-month period are free; after that, eSIMs cost $3 each within that period.
activation.byodNote: Bring Your Own Phone: the phone must be compatible (5G/4G LTE and VoLTE) and unlocked. Mint checks compatibility by IMEI.

activation.activationFeeNote: Public Mobile advertises 'no contracts, no credit checks, or hidden fees'. No activation or connection fee is listed.
activation.simKitNote: Footnote 4 on publicmobile.ca: 'Regular price for a physical SIM card is $15, and for an eSIM is $5... Prices do not include applicable taxes.'
activation.esimPromoNote: '$0 eSIM when you subscribe to any phone plan', a promotion ending 5 October 2026 for new prepaid activations.
activation.byodNote: Bring-your-own-phone only. Public Mobile runs on the TELUS network.
activation.note: In February 2024, Public Mobile community posts quoted a $10 physical SIM and a $5 eSIM. The live footnote now says $15 for a physical SIM.
